title: Goodwill, intangibles, and impairments
objectives: Answer out loud: How is goodwill created?
Answer out loud: What happens when it's impaired?
Answer out loud: Is it tax-deductible?

steps.body: When a company buys another for more than the fair value of its identifiable net assets, the excess is goodwill.
Goodwill = purchase price − fair value of net identifiable assets.
Under US GAAP (public companies), goodwill isn't amortized. It's tested for impairment at least yearly.
An impairment is a non-cash charge on the IS that reduces goodwill on the BS.

blocks.template: A goodwill impairment is a {{1}} charge
Under US GAAP, public companies {{1}} amortize goodwill

blocks.title: Why can't a company create goodwill internally?
blocks.teaser: Goodwill only exists when someone pays a market price above book value.
blocks.body: Goodwill only exists when someone pays a market price above book value. A company's own brand or culture isn't recorded as an asset, because there's no transaction to measure it.

blocks.title: What's the difference between goodwill and other intangibles?
blocks.teaser: Identifiable intangibles (customer lists, patents, trademarks) can be separated and valued.
blocks.body: Identifiable intangibles (customer lists, patents, trademarks) can be separated and valued. Most have finite lives and are amortized. Goodwill is the unidentifiable residual — synergies, workforce, reputation — and isn't amortized under US GAAP.

blocks.title: Is goodwill tax-deductible?
blocks.teaser: In a stock purchase, no — the tax basis doesn't change.
blocks.body: In a stock purchase, no — the tax basis doesn't change. In an asset purchase (or a 338(h)(10) election), the buyer gets a stepped-up basis and can amortize goodwill for tax over 15 years, which creates real tax savings.

blocks.prompt: When can a buyer amortize goodwill for tax purposes?

options.text: In an asset purchase or a 338(h)(10) election, over 15 years
Only when the goodwill is impaired

blocks.explanation: A stock purchase keeps the old tax basis, so no deduction. An asset purchase (or 338(h)(10)) steps up the basis and lets the buyer amortize goodwill for tax over 15 years.

blocks.title: What's negative goodwill?
blocks.teaser: If the buyer pays less than the fair value of net identifiable assets — a bargain purchase — the difference is recognized as a gain on the IS.
blocks.body: If the buyer pays *less* than the fair value of net identifiable assets — a bargain purchase — the difference is recognized as a gain on the IS. It's rare and usually involves distressed sellers.

blocks.title: Why do analysts often ignore impairments?
blocks.teaser: An impairment says the company overpaid for a past deal.
blocks.body:
An impairment says the company overpaid for a past deal. It's non-cash and doesn't change future cash flows, so it's excluded from adjusted EBITDA and EPS. It's still a signal about management's capital allocation.

**Interview answer:** "It's a non-cash admission of overpaying for an acquisition. It doesn't change future cash flow, so we strip it out of adjusted metrics."
